title: Policy umbrella and operator checkpoint flow for phased batching & cache activations
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Objective: Implement a policy 'umbrella' controller and an operator checkpoint flow that enables staggered activation of batching and KV-cache recommendations safely across tenants. The umbrella controller centralizes gating logic (policy evaluation, rate limits, eligiblity checks) while operator checkpoints provide reproducible audit points and manual override hooks for SRE/Operators. The feature must support staged activation windows (percent-of-traffic canaries, time-based ramps, and tenant cohorts), automated health probes, and automatic rollback criteria tied to latency/error cost SLAs. This work ties into Optimize's suggestion engine and the Console rollout UI so operators can approve/hold/abort activations. Key constraints: preserve strict tenant isolation, ensure deterministic rollback to previously pinned configs, and keep per-request latency tail within configured SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Umbrella controller that evaluates rules and emits activation tickets for candidate recommendations
Operator checkpoint API and Console surface to approve/hold/abort pending activations
Canary partitioning supports percent traffic and tenant-cohort modes with configurable ramp schedules
Automated health probes that trigger rollback when latency P99 increases > 15% or error rate increases > 2x baseline
Audit log entries (immutable) created for every activation step including operator decisions and automated rollbacks
End-to-end e2e test covering activation → canary → ramp → rollback on injected failure
Backwards compatibility with existing Dedicated and Private deployment routing policies
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature flag behind runtime-optimize-umbrella; infra canary on internal dev account. Phase 1: limited tenant cohort (5 tenants) with percent-based traffic gating and telemetry hooks. Phase 2: expand to 20% traffic across graduated cohorts with operator checkpoint required for >20%. Phase 3: general availability with configurable automatic adoption when telemetry is green for 72h. Canary windows will use synthetic traffic generation for load-sensitive checks.
failure_modes_and_mitigations: Unexpected latency spike: immediate rollback via controller + alert to ops; mitigation: reduce batch depth and revert caching TTLs
Degraded correctness / increased hallucination: operator hold and automatic revert to pinned model/config; mitigation: route affected traffic to pinned variant
State drift between controller and private deployments: detect via reconciler checksum and trigger drift remediation job
Permissions/approval deadlock: provide emergency bypass token path with audit log and TTL for SRE
